description: Structured design-principle framework for programmatic AI integration (system prompts, RAG, tool definitions). Distilled from 10 foundational UX/UI design books plus industry-standard supplementary frameworks (Nielsen's heuristics, Laws of UX, Refactoring UI, Atomic Design, WCAG 2.2, UX writing research).

operating_rules.rule: Identify the user, their task, and the actual blocker before proposing any visual or interaction change.
Every suggestion must name a specific principle and the concrete failure it prevents. Banned unattributed phrases: 'make it more modern', 'clean up the UI', 'improve the UX'.
Establish domain (e-commerce, b2b-saas, mobile-first, accessibility-critical, other) before prescribing solutions; adjust priorities per domain_priorities.
Label suggestions as principle-backed fact vs. untested assumption; propose cheap validation for risky assumptions.
Name the specific principle and book behind every piece of feedback or generated recommendation.

principles.name: affordances
principles.summary: Interactive elements must visually signal how they're used.
principles.check: Would a first-time user know what's clickable without being told?

principles.name: feedback
principles.summary: Every action needs an immediate (<100ms), visible response.
principles.check: Are loading, success, and error states visually distinct and in plain language?

principles.name: constraints
principles.summary: Prevent errors by design rather than showing an error after the fact.
principles.check: Are invalid options disabled or hidden instead of erroring on submit?

principles.name: mapping
principles.summary: Control layout should match the user's mental model, not the data model.
principles.check: Do related controls group the way users think about the task, not how the schema is structured?

principles.name: signifiers
principles.summary: The cue for an affordance must be obvious, consistent, and not color-only.
principles.check: Does the signifier survive grayscale / screen reader / first glance?

principles.name: self_evidence
principles.summary: Identity, current location, and primary action should require zero thought.
principles.check: Could a new user state the page's purpose in one glance?

principles.name: eliminate_instructions
principles.summary: If a tooltip is needed to explain a control, redesign the control instead.
principles.check: Would removing all help text/tooltips break usability?

principles.name: single_primary_action
principles.summary: One clearly dominant action per screen or section.
principles.check: Are there two or more visually equal calls to action competing for attention?

principles.name: scannability
principles.summary: Users scan, they don't read; front-load key words, use headings.
principles.check: Can the key information be gotten from headings and bolded terms alone?

principles.name: cheap_frequent_testing
principles.summary: One user testing a prototype beats a stakeholder debate.
principles.check: Has this been shown to a real user, or only discussed internally?

books.title: Designing Interfaces
books.author: Jennifer Tidwell, Charles Brewer, Aynee Valencia

principles.name: pattern_reuse
principles.summary: Reuse established interaction patterns for solved problems instead of inventing new ones.
principles.check: Is there a well-known pattern (wizard, autocomplete, card sort, etc.) for this exact problem?

principles.name: product_wide_consistency
principles.summary: Consistency across the product outweighs local optimization of one screen.
principles.check: Does this screen's pattern match how the same interaction works elsewhere in the product?

principles.name: documented_custom_patterns
principles.summary: Custom patterns need documentation to avoid drift as the product grows.
principles.check: If this pattern is custom, is it recorded anywhere for future consistency?

principles.name: design_thinking_order
principles.summary: Empathize, define the real problem, ideate broadly, prototype cheaply, test and iterate — in that order.
principles.check: Has the real problem been defined, or did the process start from a pre-chosen solution?

principles.name: diverge_before_converge
principles.summary: Generate multiple distinct approaches before narrowing to one.
principles.check: Were 2-3 meaningfully different directions considered, or just one refined?

principles.name: reframe_requests_as_problems
principles.summary: A feature request is a solution in disguise; find the underlying problem.
principles.check: What problem does this requested feature assume, and is that assumption correct?

principles.name: outcome_alignment
principles.summary: Design decisions should serve a measurable business/user outcome, not just look good.
principles.check: What metric or user outcome does this change move, specifically?

principles.name: discovery_before_delivery
principles.summary: Test risky assumptions cheaply before building the real thing.
principles.check: Has the riskiest assumption been tested with a prototype, or are we building straight to production?

principles.name: four_risks
principles.summary: Check value, usability, feasibility, and business viability risk before committing.
principles.check: Which of the four risks (value/usability/feasibility/viability) is least validated here?

principles.name: mental_state_design
principles.summary: Design responses to match the user's emotional state (bored, anxious, manic) in context.
principles.check: What is the user's likely emotional state right before this screen, and does the design account for it?

principles.name: habit_loop
principles.summary: Habits form around trigger, reward, low-friction action.
principles.check: Does this flow have a clear trigger and a fast, low-friction path to reward?

principles.name: assumption_to_method_mapping
principles.summary: Every major design assumption should map to a research method that could validate or kill it.
principles.check: What method would prove this assumption wrong, and has it been run?

principles.name: method_matches_question
principles.summary: Behavioral questions need observation, not surveyed opinions.
principles.check: Is a 'will they actually use it' question being answered with a survey instead of behavior data?

principles.name: no_leading_questions
principles.summary: Avoid hypothetical/leading questions; ask about specific past behavior instead.
principles.check: Does the validation question ask 'would you use X' instead of 'what have you done about this so far'?

principles.name: past_behavior_over_opinion
principles.summary: People are polite liars about future intent but honest about past actions.
principles.check: Is the evidence based on stated intent or on demonstrated past behavior/spend?

principles.name: evidence_of_investment
principles.summary: 'That sounds cool' isn't validation; look for money, time, or effort already spent.
principles.check: Has the user spent real money, time, or workaround effort on this problem already?

principles.name: deliberate_defaults
principles.summary: Defaults are powerful and should be chosen deliberately and transparently.
principles.check: Was the default chosen intentionally to serve the user, or is it just whatever was easiest to build?

principles.name: ethical_persuasion
principles.summary: Use social proof/scarcity/progress to help users reach their own goals, not to trick them.
principles.check: Does this persuasion technique serve the user's actual goal or only the business's?

principles.name: flag_dark_patterns
principles.summary: Explicitly avoid confirmshaming, hidden costs, forced continuity, and roach-motel patterns.
principles.check: Does this flow use any dark pattern that would embarrass the team if made public?

principles.name: invisible_ux
principles.summary: Good UX is often invisible; a noticed interface usually signals a problem.
principles.check: Did the user comment on the interface itself rather than just completing their task?

principles.name: compounding_small_fixes
principles.summary: Fix specific frictions one at a time rather than chasing an abstract 'better UX'.
principles.check: Is this feedback a concrete, fixable friction point or a vague aesthetic preference?

principles.name: visibility_of_system_status
principles.summary: Keep users informed via timely, appropriate feedback.
principles.check: Does every action produce a visible response, and can users always tell the current state?

principles.name: match_real_world
principles.summary: Speak the user's language; follow real-world conventions.
principles.check: Does copy avoid internal jargon the user wouldn't use themselves?

principles.name: user_control_and_freedom
principles.summary: Provide a clearly marked emergency exit (undo/cancel).
principles.check: Is there an obvious way to undo or cancel most actions?

principles.name: consistency_and_standards
principles.summary: Don't make users wonder if different words/actions mean the same thing.
principles.check: Are the same terms/icons used for the same concept everywhere?

principles.name: error_prevention
principles.summary: Prevent problems before they occur rather than message after.
principles.check: Does the UI disable/hide invalid options instead of letting users pick them and fail?

principles.name: recognition_over_recall
principles.summary: Minimize memory load by making options visible.
principles.check: Are choices shown rather than requiring recall from elsewhere?

principles.name: flexibility_and_efficiency
principles.summary: Offer accelerators for experts without penalizing novices.
principles.check: Are there shortcuts/batch actions for frequent tasks?

principles.name: aesthetic_minimalist_design
principles.summary: Every extra unit of information competes with relevant ones.
principles.check: Could any clutter be removed without losing function?

principles.name: help_recognize_diagnose_recover
principles.summary: Error messages in plain language stating the problem and a solution.
principles.check: Do errors avoid codes/jargon and suggest a fix?

principles.name: help_and_documentation
principles.summary: Ideally no docs needed; if required, task-oriented and searchable.
principles.check: Can most tasks be completed without consulting help?

principles.name: jakobs_law
principles.summary: Users prefer your product to work like the ones they already know.
principles.check: Does this reinvent a convention users already have from elsewhere?

principles.name: fitts_law
principles.summary: Target-acquisition time depends on size and distance.
principles.check: Are frequent/primary targets large and close to the likely cursor/thumb position?

principles.name: hicks_law
principles.summary: Decision time increases with number/complexity of choices.
principles.check: Could this choice set be reduced or organized with progressive disclosure?

principles.name: millers_law
principles.summary: Working memory holds ~7±2 items.
principles.check: Is long information chunked instead of presented as one unbroken block?

principles.name: postels_law
principles.summary: Be liberal in what you accept, conservative in what you send.
principles.check: Does input validation reject reasonable variation instead of normalizing it?

principles.name: peak_end_rule
principles.summary: Experiences are judged mainly by their peak and ending.
principles.check: Has deliberate attention gone into the final/most intense moment of this flow?

principles.name: aesthetic_usability_effect
principles.summary: Attractive designs are perceived as more usable and forgiven more.
principles.check: Is visual polish being used as a substitute for real usability testing?

principles.name: von_restorff_effect
principles.summary: The visually distinct item among similar ones is remembered best.
principles.check: Does the single primary action stand out, without over-using this or relying on color alone?

principles.name: zeigarnik_effect
principles.summary: Unfinished tasks are remembered and motivate completion.
principles.check: Does an incomplete state show visible progress toward finishing?

principles.name: serial_position_effects
principles.summary: First and last items in a series are best recalled.
principles.check: Are the most important items placed first/last, not buried in the middle?

principles.name: doherty_threshold
principles.summary: Engagement rises sharply under ~400ms response time.
principles.check: Is there an immediate loading indicator for anything likely to exceed 400ms?

principles.name: goal_gradient_effect
principles.summary: Motivation increases the closer one gets to a goal.
principles.check: Does a progress indicator start non-zero and accelerate near completion?

principles.name: law_of_common_region
principles.summary: Elements sharing a bounded area are perceived as a group.
principles.check: Are related items visually contained together?

principles.name: law_of_proximity
principles.summary: Nearby objects are perceived as related.
principles.check: Is spacing tighter within a group than between groups?

principles.name: law_of_pragnanz
principles.summary: Ambiguous shapes are perceived in their simplest form; similar elements read as one group.
principles.check: Is one consistent style used for a whole category of action (e.g. all destructive actions)?

principles.name: occams_razor
principles.summary: Prefer the solution with fewest assumptions/elements.
principles.check: Can any field/step be removed by inferring it instead of asking?

principles.name: teslers_law
principles.summary: Complexity can move between system and user but not disappear.
principles.check: When complexity is removed from the user, has it been built into the system instead?

principles.name: parkinsons_law
principles.summary: A task expands to fill the time allotted.
principles.check: Would a visible time estimate or deadline help a low-priority task get done?

principles.name: paradox_of_choice
principles.summary: Too many options degrade decision-making and satisfaction.
principles.check: Could the option set be curated to a smaller recommended default?

principles.name: cognitive_load
principles.summary: Total mental effort to use an interface, intrinsic plus extraneous.
principles.check: Is data persisted across steps so users never re-enter or re-remember it?

principles.name: chunking
principles.summary: Breaking information into meaningful groups improves recall.
principles.check: Is a long list/settings page split into labeled sections?

supplementary_frameworks.title: UX Writing & Microcopy
supplementary_frameworks.author: NN/g, Google Material, Nicely Said (Fenton & Kiefer Lee)

principles.name: verb_first_ctas
principles.summary: Button labels lead with a verb plus specific object.
principles.check: Does the button say 'Save changes' rather than 'Submit'?

principles.name: specific_error_messages
principles.summary: Errors state the specific problem in plain language with a fix, near the field.
principles.check: Does the error avoid jargon/codes and suggest what to do next?

principles.name: named_confirmation_actions
principles.summary: Confirm buttons name the actual action, not generic OK/Confirm.
principles.check: Does the destructive-action button say 'Delete order' rather than 'OK'?

principles.name: persistent_labels
principles.summary: Form fields need a persistent visible label, not a placeholder standing in for one.
principles.check: Does the label disappear when the user starts typing?

principles.name: purposeful_empty_states
principles.summary: Empty states explain why and offer one next action.
principles.check: Does the empty state say more than 'No results found'?

supplementary_frameworks.title: Visual Design Craft
supplementary_frameworks.author: Refactoring UI (Wathan & Schoger); current design criticism on generic AI/template UI

principles.name: deliberate_type_scale
principles.summary: Hand-pick a type scale rather than a rigid computed ratio.
principles.check: Do font sizes follow a consistent, deliberate scale?

principles.name: systematic_color_palette
principles.summary: Build a palette of named roles (grey/primary/accent) with hand-picked HSL shades.
principles.check: Is the palette an intentional system, or a default/decorative gradient?

principles.name: non_linear_spacing_scale
principles.summary: Use a non-linear spacing scale; group spacing should exceed internal spacing.
principles.check: Does spacing follow a scale, and does grouping read clearly from spacing alone?

principles.name: avoid_generic_ai_look
principles.summary: Avoid named anti-patterns: gradient hero, bento grid, cardocalypse borders, 3D gradient blobs, reflexive default fonts.
principles.check: Does this design hit any of the named generic-AI-look anti-patterns?

supplementary_frameworks.title: Design Systems
supplementary_frameworks.author: Atomic Design (Brad Frost); design tokens practice

principles.name: atomic_hierarchy
principles.summary: Structure UI as atoms, molecules, organisms, templates, pages.
principles.check: Is this built from reusable, composed pieces or bespoke one-off markup?

principles.name: design_tokens
principles.summary: Store color/spacing/type/radius/shadow as named variables, not hardcoded values.
principles.check: Would a rebrand or theme change require a token edit, or a find-and-replace?

principles.name: formalize_on_signal
principles.summary: Formalize a system when duplicated components, dev/design drift, or rebuild-from-scratch friction appear — not before.
principles.check: Is there real evidence of duplication/drift, or is this premature structure before product-market fit?

supplementary_frameworks.title: Admin UX for Non-Technical Users
supplementary_frameworks.author: Synthesized from NN/g, Pencil & Paper, LogRocket, and internal-tools UX practice

principles.name: design_for_least_technical_user
principles.summary: Design for the least technical person who will use this, optimizing for safety over efficiency.
principles.check: Would this design still make sense to someone anxious about making a mistake?

principles.name: destructive_action_decision_order
principles.summary: Prefer undo, then soft-delete/trash, then specific confirmation, then rare type-to-confirm — in that order.
principles.check: Is a confirmation dialog used where undo or soft-delete would serve better?

principles.name: plain_job_vocabulary
principles.summary: Use the user's own job vocabulary, not system/database terminology.
principles.check: Would this term appear in the user's own job description?

principles.name: audit_trail_as_trust
principles.summary: A visible, searchable activity log reduces fear of unrecoverable mistakes.
principles.check: Can the user see what they did and undo/trace it themselves?

principles.name: wizards_for_infrequent_tasks
principles.summary: Stepped wizards for unfamiliar/infrequent tasks; dense forms only for tasks done often.
principles.check: Is an infrequent, high-stakes task presented as a guided flow rather than a dense form?

steps: Restate the problem/goal in one sentence to confirm understanding
Identify domain context, or ask if unclear
List specific findings, each citing a named principle and book
Give a concrete, actionable fix for each finding
Flag assumptions that should be validated with real users before further design effort
